name: Tutong
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Haji Ramlee Tunggal. 2005. Struktur Bahasa Tutong. Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka Brunei
earlier_scan.note: Print-only Brunei DBP structure book; Wikipedia article has no stress statement

sources.citation: UBD FASS research pages: 'The Pronunciation of the Indigenous Languages of Brunei Darussalam' (Deterding, Gardiner, Yabit Alas, 2018-2020) and 'The Tutong Digital Dictionary project' (Clynes, Noor Azam, Ashrol Rahimy, Ramlee Tunggal, 2011-2013).
sources.note: Tutong North Wind and the Sun text and audio posted but marked '(Analysis not yet complete)'; the Dusun, Kedayan, Brunei Malay analyses exist, none for Tutong. The dictionary project page states 'there is very little published information about Bahasa Tutong, and only one small dictionary (DBPB 1991)'.

sources.citation: Noor Azam Haji-Othman. 2005. Linguistic diversity in Negara Brunei Darussalam: an ecological perspective. PhD thesis, University of Leicester.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic; the only 'stress' passage (p. 208) quotes Poedjosoedarmo 1996 on Kampung Ayer Malay, not Tutong. p. 50 lists the Tutong descriptive works: Rahim Dulani 1972, Ramlee Tunggal 1991, Mazmah Haji Mohamad Yusof 1992, DBP 1991 dictionary.

sources.citation: McLellan, James. 2014. Strategies for revitalizing endangered Borneo languages: a comparison between Negara Brunei Darussalam and Sarawak, Malaysia. Southeast Asia: A Multidisciplinary Journal 14: 14-22.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; cites Noor Azam (in press) 'Teaching an unwritten language: Tutong language' (BRC volume) and DBP 2011 Daftar leksikal 7 dialek.

sources.citation: Clynes, Adrian. 2012. Dominant language transfer in minority language documentation projects: some examples from Brunei. Language Documentation & Conservation 6: 253-267.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; names Haji Ramlee Tunggal 2005 as the Tutong description (p. 255) and discusses the UBD Tutong documentation/dictionary project.

sources.citation: Nothofer, Bernd. 1991. The languages of Brunei Darussalam. In H. Steinhauer (ed.), Papers in Austronesian Linguistics No. 1, 151-176. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics A-81.
sources.note: Tutong section (pp. 154-155) gives speaker numbers, dialect variation in final voiced stops, lexicostatistics and a Swadesh list; nothing on stress or accent for any language.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en/ms/id), 'Tutong language' / 'Bahasa Tutong', phonology section citing DBP 1991 Kamus Tutong-Melayu.
sources.note: Vowel and consonant tables only; no statement on stress.
